outcome: No result since 26 January 2024 settles, advances a bound on, or resolves a genuine restriction of the stated reciprocity law for k-th order norm residues; the problem remains open and is uniformly described (Wikipedia's article, a June 2026 Simons Foundation survey of all 23 Hilbert problems, and standard framing) as tied to non-abelian class field theory / the Langlands program, still unresolved.
summary: Hilbert's ninth problem asks for the most general reciprocity law for k-th order norm residues in a general algebraic number field, for k a prime power. The abelian case is settled by classical class field theory / Artin reciprocity (long before the window), but the general (non-abelian) case is universally treated as open, folded into non-abelian class field theory and the Langlands program. I checked the problem's own Wikipedia article (last substantive content unchanged in relevant part: 'Despite some results towards Langlands program, this conjecture seems to be far from proven, but stands as the best proposition of solution for Hilbert's ninth problem'), a June 2026 Simons Foundation survey of the status of all 23 Hilbert problems (which explicitly calls the ninth problem's status 'It's complicated' and says 'A great deal of progress has been made on this and the closely related 12th problem over the years, but neither is completely resolved' — giving no dated post-2024 event), and arXiv listings for 'Hilbert's ninth problem' and 'non-abelian class field theory' from 2024-2026. Two 2025 papers turned up that use the phrase 'non-abelian class field theory' — S. Bedikyan, 'Local non-abelian class field theory' (Hacettepe J. Math. Stat., published 28 April 2025), which extends İkeda–Serbest's local reciprocity map construction to any local field with a p-th root of unity, and I. V. Nikolaev's 2025 Algebras and Representation Theory paper relating Drinfeld modules to noncommutative tori. Both are incremental contributions to the broader non-abelian class field theory program (itself a decades-old research direction, not new since 2024) rather than results that a careful reader would record as advancing Hilbert's ninth problem's own stated bullet: neither claims a general reciprocity law for norm residues of k-th order over a general number field, and Bedikyan's result is local (p-adic fields), a restriction of scope rather than a step toward the general global statement Hilbert asked for, and its own framing situates it as one more contribution to an existing multi-decade line (Koch, Fesenko, Koch–de Shalit, İkeda–Serbest) rather than a new advance dated to the window. I also confirmed that the substantial 2024-2026 arXiv activity found under 'Hilbert's [ninth/tenth] problem' searches (Koymans–Pagano, Alpöge–Bhargava–Ho–Shnidman, etc.) is entirely on Hilbert's tenth problem (Diophantine decidability), a different problem, and does not bear on the ninth. No source anywhere discusses AI/LLM involvement in any work touching this problem; the only AI-adjacent hits were a 2025 Apple ML paper named 'Hilbert' (an LLM+Lean proving framework, unrelated in subject) and general LLM-for-formal-mathematics papers, none of which mention this problem.
competing_reading: One could argue the Bedikyan 2025 paper on local non-abelian class field theory is a genuine 'case' of the problem (the local, prime-power-root-of-unity case) rather than a 'related' variant, since it does construct an explicit local reciprocity map satisfying functoriality and ramification properties — which is precisely the kind of object Hilbert's ninth problem asks for, just restricted to local fields. Under that reading the status would be `partial` with `resolution_direction: confirmed` (a local reciprocity law constructed) rather than `open`. I did not adopt this reading because the paper extends an existing construction (İkeda–Serbest, itself pre-2024) to a broader class of local fields rather than settling new territory of the *global*, general-number-field statement Hilbert posed, and because no secondary source (Wikipedia, Simons Foundation survey) treats any 2024-2026 work as movement on Hilbert's ninth problem specifically — both continue to describe it as essentially untouched. This is a judgment call about how much extension counts as 'a case settled' versus 'the same open research program continuing as it always has.'
what_would_settle_it: A statement, by an author or a survey (e.g., a future Simons Foundation or Notices of the AMS update), that a specific 2024+ paper newly settles a well-defined case or sub-case of the general k-th order norm residue reciprocity law (as opposed to a general contribution to the decades-long non-abelian class field theory program), together with that paper's date and scope.
